tweet_summary: Niche Yakuza-fan account 'Judgement Kazzer' (bio: 'most miserable Yakuza fan | slop sommelier | #REMOVEKAGAWA') posts a fan-made video styled as a Like A Dragon 9 trailer, captioned 'BREAKING: The first official Like a Dragon 9 story trailer has seemingly leaked online. (Via: @IGN)'.
why_note_decision: This is obvious in-community satire from a self-described 'slop sommelier' niche-Yakuza-comedy account. Top replies confirm: 'Pre-order Like a Dragon 9: The Rise of Yakuza to get the legendary Ichiban Kasuga Manager DLC for Kiryu's Orphanage Builder Minigame!', 'No Ichiban in sight #Yep #ItsReal', 'No community note must be real', 'It unironically is actually gonna end up being as ungrounded as this lmao'. The 'Via: @IGN' is the joke. There is no real Like A Dragon 9 trailer, but no one is being misled — the audience is in on the bit. Writing a literal debunk on community comedy is a classic false positive.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note; any note here is a false positive. The tweet is in-community satire from a niche Yakuza-fan parody account, and top replies make explicit the audience is in on the joke (mocking the fake-trailer trope, joking about a community note, etc.). A bot must distinguish niche-community satire/jokes from genuine misinformation — a literal debunk like the original is the failure mode to avoid.

original_unhelpful_note.text: This is a fan-made trailer; no official Like a Dragon 9 has been announced and IGN has not reported any such leak. https://ryu-ga-gotoku.com/asia_en https://www.ign.com/search?q=Like+a+Dragon+9

fact_check.notes: Fan-made/joke trailer. Account bio + replies make this unambiguously a community-comedy post, not a sincere claim.

importance.lens_rationale: Low impressions, niche gaming subculture in-joke. Pipeline learning: parody accounts joking with the audience aren't misinformation.
